newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: AXA Life launches Singapore multi-fund product.
newsitem.headline: AXA Life launches Singapore multi-fund product.

text.p: AXA Life Insurance Co Ltd, a Singapore unit of French insurance giant AXA-UAP Group, on Thursday launched what it said was Singapore's first multi-fund investment-linked savings plan.
AXA Life said in a statement its Investors' Choice product would give a choice of four sub-funds to allow investors to create their own portfolio mix.
"This product makes use of the fund of funds concept that has been very well received in other parts of the world but is untried in Singapore so far," an AXA Life spokeswoman told Reuters.
It accesses the global investment market through funds investing in a combination of globally diversified fixed interest securities and equities, the spokeswoman said.

Investment-linked insurance products were launched in Singapore in 1992 and have boomed since the government allowed money saved under its compulsory Central Provident Fund (CPF) retirement plan to be invested in unit-linked products.

Industry sources believe more than Singapore $1.0 billion has been pumped into unit-linked insurance products since 1993 and predict another S$2.0 billion will be committed over the next three years as scheme rules are further relaxed.
Investment-linked plans using CPF funds are strictly regulated and must only invest in approved instruments.
Investors' Choice offers a CPF-approved portfolio to cater for both CPF and non-CPF investors. The minimum investment is S$5,000.

The plan also offers life insurance at 125 percent of the initial investment plus top-ups less withdrawals. The death benefit increases to 250 percent on accidental death before age 65, or a minimum of S$10,000. The policy matures at age 80.
Investors' Choice joins the Fortress Fund as AXA Life's second investment-linked product in Singapore.

AXA Life claims to be the sixth biggest life insurer in Singapore with a market share of about 1.55 percent. The 14 players in the market wrote S$4.2 billion in new premiums in 1996, according to figures from the Insurance Commissioner.
